summary:
Terra Twin is an interactive web app that searches the whole Earth for places that resemble Moon and Mars exploration sites. It scores about 318,000 land cells against Artemis south-pole regions and Jezero crater on 17 traits, including terrain, temperature, sunlight, dryness, ice, vegetation and soil moisture, using open NASA, JAXA and ESA data. Users choose from six mission-based ranking methods or set custom trait weights. A radar chart and a points breakdown show what matches and what doesn’t. The top ten matches are then re-ranked on an 8 km landing zone using 30 m terrain data, and the app flags promising places far from known analog sites.
It addresses the challenge by searching globally and systematically instead of only rediscovering famous sites, and by explaining each match and its limits, such as gravity, vacuum and radiation.
It matters because testing rovers, habitats and procedures on Earth is far cheaper than doing it in space, and a better-matched site means more realistic training and technology tests. We validated the scoring against known analog sites, with an AUC of about 0.74 for Mars and 0.76 for the Moon.
details:
Terra Twin is a web app that searches all of Earth for places that resemble Moon and Mars exploration sites. You pick a target: the Artemis III south-pole base regions on the Moon, or Jezero crater on Mars. The app describes the target with 17 traits (terrain slope and roughness, temperature, day-night swing, sun angle, dryness, ice, vegetation, soil moisture, dust, rock type and more). It then scores about 318,000 land cells of roughly 28 km against it. You choose one of six mission-based ranking methods, such as rover and landing tests or polar base, or set custom trait weights. A radar chart and a points breakdown show what matches and what doesn't. The top ten are re-ranked by sliding an 8 km landing zone over 30 m terrain data. Each result has a "how to use this site" card and a "limits" line (gravity, vacuum, radiation and thin atmosphere cannot be reproduced on Earth). Promising places far from the 107 known analog sites are flagged as new candidates.

Testing rovers, habitats and procedures on Earth is far cheaper than in space, and a better-matched site means more realistic training and technology tests. The tool lets mission planners find analogs systematically, for a specific purpose, instead of reusing the famous sites, and it is open and explainable.

Plain JavaScript, HTML and CSS running entirely in the browser from a data pack of about 6 MB, with no server. Python for data processing. Open data from NASA (POWER, MERRA-2, LRO LOLA and Diviner, MOLA, TES, Perseverance MEDA weather), JAXA (GCOM-C, GSMaP, JASMES), ESA (WorldCover), AWS Terrain Tiles and the GLiM lithology map. Built with Claude Code and hosted from GitHub.

It reverses the usual question: instead of checking one known analog, it scores the whole planet against a chosen mission purpose. It also shows why a place matches and where the analogy fails.

We validated the scoring against 72 known analog sites (AUC about 0.74 for Mars and 0.76 for the Moon, on a scale where 0.5 is chance), found and fixed a data bug above 82.75°N and an ice-sheet bias in the Moon rankings, and used real Perseverance weather for Jezero. We state the limits openly: the 30 m step validates at about 0.68, Moon target points are approximate, tolerances are expert estimates, and some traits (dust, ice, soil moisture) mean different things off Earth.
projectRefs: USGS Unified Geologic Map of the Moon
